title: Mismatch and edge-case log — hiring scratch for Juno Park
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick personal notes after loop with Juno Park (runtime architect candidate). This is a raw scratchpad — unpolished, stream-of-thought. Use for panel sync + vote prep.

Topline impression (high level):
- Strong on latency-oriented heuristics and kernel trade-offs; good intuition for batching and KV cache behavior.
- Some gaps on system-level observability and incident postmortem specificity (how they'd debug perf regressions in noisy prod).
- Architecture instincts skew more "practical" than "foundational" — likes hacks that buy latency wins quickly. That’s OK depending on role.

Concrete positives:
- Pairing exercise: implemented a working prefix-cache shim and reasoned about memory growth and TTLs. Wrote compact pseudo-code and caught the O(N) traversal risk when evicting stale prefixes.
- Latency cost tradeoff: proposed a hybrid cache (per-customer hot list + global LRU) and articulated when skyline of cost favors one vs the other.
- Good breadth on quantization impacts (noted 8-bit asymmetric vs 4-bit group size tradeoffs) and how it interacts with kernel selection.

Mismatches and edge cases (things that worried me):
- Observability and instrumentation: their plan relied on ad hoc counters and distributed spans but lacked concrete SLIs to triage model divergence vs infra regressions. Example: when top-k sampling latency jumps, they defaulted to "more profiling" instead of actionable rollback/runbook flow.
- Canary/rollout thinking: comfortable with canarying model parameters but less clear on rollout automation (how to wire the automated fallback to an older quantized variant under memory pressure).
- Kubernetes vs bare-metal nuance: lacked concrete examples of when to prefer node-level NUMA binding or MIG splits versus multi-tenancy scheduling policies. Couldn’t cite a previous production migration with metrics.

Edge-case scenarios I asked about (and answers):
1) Sudden throughput drop caused by long-tail sequences:
   - Juno: prefer priority queues + request trimming for non-critical requests. Also suggested dynamic batching thresholds.
   - My note: good mitigation, but how do you avoid systematic quality degradation? Need more on QoS tiers and SLA mapping.
2) KV cache leak when model versioning changes hidden key shapes:
   - Juno: suggested namespace + version tags and a lazy invalidation pass.
   - My note: fine as a patch, but risk of thundering refresh on first requests — missing circuit-breaker plan.
3) Hot customer causing eviction storms:
   - Juno: keep per-customer cap + backpressure to client.
   - My note: acceptable but operationalizing backpressure needs API hooks + clear client contract — they glossed over that.

Behavioral / collaboration notes:
- Communicates clearly under pressure, asks targeted clarification questions during ambiguous prompts.
- Willing to change approach when given data, not dogmatic.
- Some tendency to jump to implementation specifics early; could benefit from pausing for higher-level failure-mode analysis.

Quick scorecard (my internal numbers, for panel use):
- System design: 7/10
- Runtime internals / kernels: 8/10
- Observability & SRE integration: 5/10
- Product sense / tradeoffs: 7/10
- Communication: 8/10
- Overall recommendation: strong candidate for a senior engineer on runtime team, borderline for lead/architect until SRE + rollout gaps are addressed.

Open questions / follow-ups to ask panel or next interview if we keep them: 
- Ask for a specific postmortem-style prompt: "The 99th percentile token latency doubled after a deploy. Walk me through the drill from detection to mitigation to long-term fix." Watch for runbook specificity, data queries, rollback criteria.
- Have them sketch an automated fallback pipeline: what metrics trigger fallback, how to validate correctness of fallback, how to avoid oscillation across variants.
- Ask about a concrete migration they led (k8s -> bare-metal or vice versa) with measurable outcomes.

Operational risk flags (short):
- Lacks concrete rollback automation detail — risk during high-stakes deploys.
- Might under-index on cost signals; tends to focus on latency wins without quantifying token-unit cost impact.

Suggested interview outcome / next steps:
- If panel leans hire: pair them with an SRE-focused follow-up (incident & rollout engineering) rather than a second pure pairing. That will surface the observability/runbook gaps quickly.
- OR: hire at Senior Engineer level with a 6-month growth plan to own rollout automation and SRE integrations.

Misc notes / random scribbles:
- Liked the phrase they used: "optimistic eviction with a safety leash" — succinct and operational.
- Pairing code style: compact, typed pseudocode, favored readability over micro-optimizations (ok).
- Seemed excited about open-source benchmarking tools; might be a good contributor to our internal perf harness.

Action items (for me):
- Drop these notes into panel thread before the sync (INF-hiring).
- Prep the postmortem prompt and send to Diego + Maya to include in the follow-up interview plan.
- Flag JIRA INF-6412 as the follow-up ticket for an SRE-style session.

End of scratchpad.

-- Asha
